headline: Multi-omics signatures stratify tumor prognosis and immune context across cancers
label: Cancer Multiomics Prognostic Signatures
summary: Integrated transcriptomic and single-cell datasets are increasingly used to derive prognostic signatures and candidate regulators in tumors.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational stratification of tumors from public transcriptomic cohorts, with prognostic signatures built from TCGA and GEO data in lung adenocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, breast and ovarian cancer, and linked to immune profiles and predicted drug response. Several items extend this to single-cell and spatial resolution: a >2M-cell CTCL atlas from 116 patients, CHPF and GPC1 as markers of cancer-associated fibroblast-dominant spatial domains in colorectal cancer, and a CREM-centric regulon in HCC T cells whose coupling to expression depends on activation state and isoform usage. The SCITRAM preprint addresses the upstream step by inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomes to nominate master transcription factors. What is new is less the signature paradigm itself than the emphasis on regulon-level and cell-state-dependent readouts, which suggests that bulk-derived expression signatures may not map cleanly onto regulatory activity.
